Mission.text: Our mission is to strive to build and maintain a learning community that develops leaders through faith, knowledge and ingenuity.

Vision.title: Vision
Vision.text: Calgary Islamic School strives to develop an enriched learning community that promotes academic achievement, leadership and Islamic values.

Beliefs.title: Beliefs
Beliefs.text: We believe in the oneness of God (Allah), the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him), and the Quran as the final revelation. Islamic principles guide our educational approach, emphasizing moral character, personal development, and lifelong learning. Education is a shared responsibility between the school, parents, and the community, working together to nurture students who embody Islamic values while achieving academic excellence.

AkramJomaaPage.text3: The Whole Child, The Whole Way
AkramJomaaPage.text5: Akram Jomaa Islamic School is a K-12 institution serving over 1,000 students with more than 70 dedicated staff members. We provide a welcoming and caring learning environment inspired by the rich ethos of Islam, aimed at cultivating spiritually mature, strong Canadian Muslims.
AkramJomaaPage.text6: In partnership with Prairie Rose Public Schools (formalized June 2025), we continue as a crucial alternative education program within the public school system, significantly enhancing educational opportunities while honoring our religious beliefs, values, and diverse cultures.
AkramJomaaPage.text8: Aligned with Prairie Rose Public Schools' goals to ignite minds, forge futures, and kindle hearts
AkramJomaaPage.text10: Students demonstrate literacy competencies to participate fully and successfully in living, learning, and work. We implement the science of reading, disciplinary literacy, and effective writing strategies.
AkramJomaaPage.text12: Students demonstrate the ability, confidence, and willingness to engage with quantitative or spatial information to make informed decisions in all aspects of daily living.
AkramJomaaPage.text14: Students demonstrate knowledge, skills, and experiences to improve health and well-being across five domains: Spiritual, Intellectual, Physical, Social, and Emotional.
AkramJomaaPage.text16: At Akram Jomaa, we endeavor to be people of Ihsan (Spiritual Excellence) by embodying seven core values: Sincerity, Trustworthiness, Compassion, Courage, Patience, Gratitude, and Humility.
AkramJomaaPage.text17: We believe that acquiring knowledge is a foundational attribute of the human being and that every student has the capacity to learn and grow. Our teachers follow in the footsteps of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), cognizant of their professional role, religious responsibility, and spiritual significance.
AkramJomaaPage.text18: We serve a remarkably diverse community of learners from various African, Middle Eastern, and South Asian countries, unified by their high motivation to succeed in academic and religious pursuits.

BudgetTransparencyPage.text3: A message from the CISS Board of Directors
BudgetTransparencyPage.text5: Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh dear parents,
BudgetTransparencyPage.text6: We sincerely thank you for your engagement, your candid feedback, and your continued commitment to Calgary Islamic School. The level of involvement reflects a shared responsibility for the success of our school and the well-being of our children.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text7: Following the recent town hall, we understand that many parents have concerns regarding the fee adjustment for the 2026–2027 academic year, as well as questions related to transparency, process, and communication. These are valid concerns, and we are committed to addressing them clearly and constructively.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text9: The fee adjustment was developed through a detailed review of the school's operating requirements and submitted through the appropriate process, including review and approval by Prairie Rose School Division.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text10: We recognize that while the approval process was followed, parent communication and engagement should have been earlier and clearer. This is an area we are actively improving.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text12: The 2026–2027 budget reflects the actual cost of delivering both academic and Islamic programming.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text23: Staffing remains the largest component of the budget. Teaching staff alone represent approximately $2.0 million. When combined with support staff and student services (including but not limited to Alternative Program education assistance, janitorial, day porters, caretakers, maintenance staff and security), staffing represents the largest portion of total costs required to deliver the program.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text31: Alberta Education O&M allocation to CISS (based on 1545 students)
BudgetTransparencyPage.text32: Remaining Budget to be Funded (A - B = C)
BudgetTransparencyPage.text34: Weighted Average Fee per Student (C / D)
BudgetTransparencyPage.text42: The cost of a Non-Certificated Teacher includes more than base salary. It reflects the full employer cost required to employ qualified staff, including vacation pay, CPP, EI, health benefits, and pension contributions. These are standard across the education sector.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text43: For example, a teacher with a base salary of $75,000 represents a total employer cost of approximately $100,000 once these required contributions are included.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text44: This reflects the true cost of delivering instruction and is consistent with standard employment practices across schools.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text45: Our Non-Certificated Teachers play a critical role in delivering Islamic, Arabic, and Quranic instruction. Ensuring they are fairly compensated is essential to maintaining program quality, stability, and continuity for our students.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text46: Furthermore, the school operates within leased facilities, and these costs form part of the day-to-day operating requirements necessary to deliver the program (including but not limited to lease payment, cleaning supplies, waste disposal, general maintenance and repairs, insurance and utilities). For context, the lease rate is significantly below typical market rates, and the total reflects the size of the space required to operate a full school program.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text47: Please note the majority of the lease value is dedicated to improving the school campuses.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text49: Alternative program fees are intended to cover costs directly related to delivering the programs that are
BudgetTransparencyPage.text51: Alberta Education provides Operations and Maintenance (O&M) funding to Prairie Rose School Division to support the basic operation and upkeep of school facilities. This funding is allocated at the division level and is based primarily on student enrollment.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text52: As part of this structure, approximately $1 million in O&M funding is applied to support the operation of Calgary Islamic School. This funding helps offset facility and operational costs; however, it does not fully cover the total cost of operating the school, which is approximately $4.7 million annually.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text53: The Board's Authority to Set School Fees
BudgetTransparencyPage.text54: CISS was registered as a not-for-profit organization on September 4, 2024, and subsequently obtained charitable status effective January 15, 2026.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text55: The Board of Directors operates under a formal governance framework established by the Societies Act (Alberta, RSA 2000, c S-14) and the Society's Bylaws, which were adopted on October 27, 2025.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text56: Section 15 of the CISS Bylaws expressly grants the Board this authority:
BudgetTransparencyPage.text57: "The Board shall determine School Fees payable each school year. Parents shall be notified in writing of such fees for the forthcoming [year] no later than April 1 of each year."
BudgetTransparencyPage.text58: "School Fees" is a defined term in the Bylaws and includes tuition fees, activity or trip fees, technology fees, capital improvement fees, alternative program fees, and any other ancillary fees. The power to set these fees rests exclusively with the Board of Directors and does not require a membership vote or referendum. This is consistent with how not-for-profit societies in Alberta are governed, where operational financial decisions are entrusted to the elected and appointed board.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text59: The Board exercised this authority following a thorough review of the Society's financial position, operating requirements, and the needs of the school community. The fee adjustment was passed by Board resolution and is effective for the upcoming school year.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text61: The Board of Directors is responsible for ensuring the financial sustainability of the school, overseeing operations, and setting school fees in accordance with the Society's Bylaws and governance framework.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text62: The Board includes parent representation, with a majority of current members being parents of students within the school, including individuals who represent the parent body. This structure is intended to ensure that parent perspectives are part of Board-level discussions and decision-making.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text63: We recognize that while representation exists at the Board level, broader parent communication and engagement should have been stronger. We are committed to improving this moving forward through more structured and consistent communication.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text65: CISS has been taking steps to establish more structured communication processes with parents. In response to recent feedback, we are accelerating these efforts through the following actions:
BudgetTransparencyPage.text66: Establishing a structured communication channel through an official website to support ongoing engagement with the Board
BudgetTransparencyPage.text67: Sharing the Society's Bylaws and governance documents on the official website
BudgetTransparencyPage.text68: Providing a clear financial summary, with financial statements shared in accordance with fiscal timelines
BudgetTransparencyPage.text69: Sharing relevant materials that are important to parents
BudgetTransparencyPage.text70: We are currently organizing this information and will share it through our new CISS website (cissociety.ca), which is under development and expected to be available in the coming weeks.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text72: The Board of Directors serves this community voluntarily. Every Director — elected or appointed — receives no remuneration. Our singular focus is the success and wellbeing of your children and the long-term sustainability of this school as a premier Islamic educational institution in Calgary.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text73: We are building something meaningful here — a school rooted in Islamic values, academic excellence, and a deep love of the Quran. That mission requires a sound financial foundation, and this fee adjustment is part of ensuring that foundation remains strong.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text74: We thank you for your patience, your candour, and your continued commitment to this school community. If you have further questions or wish to discuss this matter directly, please do not hesitate to reach out to the school office or any member of the Board.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text75: We ask Allah (SWT) to guide us and grant us wisdom in serving this community.
BudgetTransparencyPage.text76: Wassalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh,
BudgetTransparencyPage.text80: We welcome your feedback and are here to address any questions you may have.

FAQs.faq1_intro: Tuition increases are driven primarily by:
FAQs.faq1_bullet1: Staffing costs (teachers, educational assistants, and support staff)
FAQs.faq1_bullet2: Program delivery (Arabic, Islamic studies, Tahfeeth, and other specialized programs)
FAQs.faq1_bullet3: Facility and operational costs (rent, maintenance, utilities)
FAQs.faq1_bullet4: General cost increases (supplies, transportation, and insurance)
FAQs.faq1_answer: Staffing represents the largest portion of overall expenses.
FAQs.faq2_question: Why was this not communicated earlier?
FAQs.faq2_intro: We acknowledge that communication should have occurred earlier and more clearly. Going forward, we will:
FAQs.faq2_bullet1: Provide advance notice of any changes
FAQs.faq3_question: What improvements will families see as a result of the increase?
FAQs.faq3_bullet1: Greater staffing stability and reduced classroom disruptions
FAQs.faq3_bullet3: Improvements to student experience (including supervision and programming)
FAQs.faq3_answer: We recognize that some of these improvements are not yet visible and are working to address this.
FAQs.faq4_question: Why do fees appear similar to private schools?
FAQs.faq4_answer: While the school receives some public funding, additional programs—particularly Arabic, Islamic studies, and specialized programming—require resources that are not fully covered by that funding.
FAQs.faq5_question: Why are some programs (e.g., Tahfeeth) priced differently?
FAQs.faq5_answer: We will provide clearer explanations of program-specific pricing.
FAQs.faq6_question: Are there supports for families facing financial difficulty?
FAQs.faq6_intro: We understand the financial impact on families and are currently reviewing:
FAQs.faq6_bullet3: Considerations for families with multiple children
FAQs.faq6_answer: Further updates will be shared shortly.
FAQs.faq7_question: Why are field trips and activities costly?
FAQs.faq7_intro: Costs may include transportation, facility access, and third-party providers.
FAQs.faq7_answer: We are reviewing these costs and exploring ways to reduce the financial impact where possible.
FAQs.faq8_bullet2: Clear communication timelines for major decisions
FAQs.faq8_bullet3: A more structured process for addressing parent questions
FAQs.faq9_question: How are decisions made by the school/board?
FAQs.faq9_answer: We are working to provide greater transparency into these processes.
FAQs.faq10_question: Will fees continue to increase in future years?
FAQs.faq10_intro: Our goal is to improve stability and predictability in tuition planning.
FAQs.faq10_answer: We will provide clearer forward-looking guidance to help families plan ahead.

RegistrationPage.title: Registration 2026-2027
RegistrationPage.subtitle: Application process and program fees for Akram Jomaa and Omar Bin Al-Khattab campuses
RegistrationPage.notice1: Prairie Rose Public Schools and the Calgary Islamic School Society are sharing an update regarding the 2026-2027 application process and alternative program fees for the Akram Jomaa and Omar Bin Al-Khattab campuses.
RegistrationPage.notice2: At the recommendation of the Calgary Islamic School Society, the Prairie Rose Public Schools Board of Trustees approved an adjustment to alternative program fees for the 2026-2027 school year. The change reflects the continued growth of the program and the increasing complexity of Arabic, Qur'anic, and Islamic studies instruction, where students may be learning at different proficiency levels and require additional support. It also helps ensure fees remain aligned and competitive with similar faith-based and alternative programs in the Calgary region.
RegistrationPage.declaration_text: A $250 deposit (non-refundable) is required for current students and is applied toward the total annual program fee.
RegistrationPage.new_student_text: Require a $50 non-refundable application fee, with an additional $100 assessment fee for kindergarten applicants.
